name: Economist
title: Economist (Indian Economic Service)
intro: From Class 12 to the Indian Economic Service or a policy career: BA/B.Sc Economics, MA Economics, the UPSC IES/ISS exam, then ministries, RBI, research institutes or private firms.

phases.title: Class 12 (Maths helps)
phases.summary: Any stream; Maths keeps top economics programmes open.
points: Science, Commerce and Arts students are all eligible.
Maths at Class 12 helps a lot for economics degrees at the most selective colleges.
Most strong programmes and IES papers use maths and statistics.

phases.title: BA / B.Sc Economics
phases.summary: Build micro, macro and statistics basics.
points: Build microeconomics, macroeconomics and statistics foundations.
You cannot sit IES with only a bachelor's degree.
Keep maths and statistics strong for the postgraduate stage.

phases.title: MA Economics
phases.summary: Needed for IES and most economist roles.
points: IES needs a postgraduate degree in Economics, Applied Economics, Business Economics or Econometrics.
Banks, consultancies and rating agencies hire economists with a master's.
Other routes: RBI Grade B (DEPR), and UGC-NET for research and teaching.

phases.title: UPSC IES/ISS exam
phases.summary: General English, General Studies and economics papers, then an interview.
points: UPSC runs one examination for the Indian Economic Service and the Indian Statistical Service.
IES papers: General English, General Studies and economics papers, followed by an interview.
Age limits and relaxations are in the current UPSC notice; IES is separate from the Civil Services (IAS) exam.

phases.title: IES or other routes
phases.summary: Union ministries, NITI Aayog, RBI, research institutes, banks and consultancies.
points: IES entry: Group A central services start at Level 10 of the 7th CPC pay matrix (₹56,100 entry basic), plus DA, HRA and other allowances.
Government: Union ministries (finance, commerce and others), NITI Aayog, statistical and planning bodies; senior IES officers reach adviser-level posts.
Private and research: banks, rating agencies, consultancies, think tanks and universities.
